arxiv-2101-03547.title: What sunspots are whispering about covid-19?
arxiv-2101-03547.creator: Mariam M. Morchiladze, Tamila K. Silagadze, Zurab K. Silagadze
arxiv-2101-03547.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Mariam M. Morchiladze, Tamila K. Silagadze, Zurab K. Silagadze. Several studies point to the antimicrobial effects of ELF electromagnetic fields. Such fields have accompanied life from the very beginning, and it is possible that they played a significant role in its emergence and evolution. However, the literature on the biological effects of ELF electromagnetic fields is controversial, and we still lack an understanding of the complex mechanisms that make such effects, observed in many experiments, possible.

arxiv-2103-04139.title: visTree: Visualization of Subgroups for a Decision Tree
arxiv-2103-04139.creator: A. Venkatasubramaniam, J. Wolfson
arxiv-2103-04139.description: Abstract Decision trees are flexible prediction models which are constructed to quantify outcome-covariate relationships and characterize relevant population subgroups. However, the standard graphical representation of fitted decision trees highlights individual split points, and hence is suboptimal for visualizing defined subgroups.

arxiv-2109-08959.title: Soft QCD results from ALICE
arxiv-2109-08959.description: Abstract High-energy hadronic collisions are dominated by soft interactions with low momentum transfers. The description of these processes typically relies on phenomenological models. The soft QCD measurements, such as characterisation of the underlying event (UE) and study of light flavored hadrons, provide important constraints on the model parameters.

arxiv-2408-05787.title: On Zero-shot Learning in Neural State Estimation of Power Distribution Systems
arxiv-2408-05787.creator: Aleksandr Berezin 1 , Stephan Balduin 1 , Eric MSP Veith 1 , Thomas Oberließen 2 and Sebastian Peter 2
arxiv-2408-05787.description: Abstract This paper addresses the challenge of neural state estimation in power distribution systems. We identified a research gap in the current state of the art, which lies in the inability of models to adapt to changes in the power grid, such as loss of sensors and branch switching, in a zero-shot fashion.

arxiv-2408-12369.title: RoundTable: Leveraging Dynamic Schema and Contextual Autocomplete for Enhanced Query Precision in Tabular Question Answering
arxiv-2408-12369.creator: Pratyush Kumar, Kuber Vijaykumar Bellad, Bharat Vadlamudi, Aman Chadha
arxiv-2408-12369.description: Abstract With advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs), a major use case that has emerged is querying databases in plain English, translating user questions into executable database queries, which has improved significantly. However, real-world datasets often feature a vast array of attributes and complex values, complicating the LLM’s task of accurately identifying relevant columns or values from natural language queries.

arxiv-2509-07712.title: A mathematical model of vaccine hesitancy: Analysing the impact of political trends and the interaction across age and education groups in the USA
arxiv-2509-07712.creator: Wajid Ali 1 † ∗ {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0001-5533-1315}{\orcidlogo}1\dagger*} , Javad Mohamadichamgavi 2 † {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0001-7208-5996}{\orcidlogo}2\dagger} , Juan Marcos Ramírez ​ 3 {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-0000-1073}{\orcidlogo}3} , Jose Aguilar ​ 3 , 4 {}^{\lx@orcidlink{0000-0003-4194
arxiv-2509-07712.description: Abstract Vaccination against the SARS-CoV-2 disease has significantly reduced its mortality rate and spread. However, despite its availability, a considerable proportion of the public has either refused or delayed getting vaccinated. This reluctance is known as vaccine hesitancy . The aim of this paper is to present a mathematical model to investigate how social interaction can impact vaccine hesitancy.

arxiv-2509-17339.title: Comment on Frank Porter, “Confidence intervals for the Poisson distribution”
arxiv-2509-17339.creator: Robert D. Cousins
arxiv-2509-17339.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Robert D. Cousins. Frank Porter has recently posted a review of “Confidence intervals for the Poisson distribution” (arXiv:2509.02852). The long, diverse history of such intervals is closely related to that of confidence intervals for the parameter of the binomial distribution. While much of Porter’s paper is enlightening and food for thought, I believe that his discussion of the intervals advocated by Gary Feldman and myself (FC) based on the likelihood ratio test (arXiv:physics/9711021) is flawed.

pmc-10737840.title: NON-COVID-19 UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION DECREASES DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
pmc-10737840.creator: Alec Pruchnicki
pmc-10737840.description: During the Covid 19 pandemic, the Vista on 5th Assisted Living Facility in New York City instituted a wide variety of pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions (NPIs) to control the spread of the disease. Before and after vaccines were available for Covid 19, this combination of approaches reduced the usual seasonal variation of non-Covid upper respiratory infections (URIs).

pmc-11647470.title: Image navigator–based, automated coronary magnetic resonance angiography for the detection of coronary artery stenosis
pmc-11647470.creator: Gregory Wood, Reza Hajhosseiny, Alexandra Uglebjerg Pedersen, Simon Littlewood, Tina Juul Hansen, Radhouene Neji, Karl P Kunze, Jens Wetzl, Bjarne Linde Nørgaard, Jesper Møller Jensen, Michael Maeng, Per Lav Madsen, Niels Vejlstrup, Claudia Prieto, René M Botnar, Won Yong Kim
pmc-11647470.description: BackgroundCoronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) is recommended as the first-line diagnostic imaging modality in low-to-intermediate-risk individuals suspected of stable coronary artery disease (CAD). However, CCTA exposes patients to ionizing radiation and potentially nephrotoxic contrast agents. Invasive coronary angiography is the gold-standard investigation to guide coronary revascularisation strategy; however, invasive procedures incur an inherent risk to the patient.

pmc-11688967.title: STRATEGIES USED BY STAFF TO PROVIDE PERSON-CENTERED DEMENTIA CARE: A COMPARISON BY LENGTH OF TENURE
pmc-11688967.creator: Yoon Chung Kim, Michael Lepore, Nancy Kusmaul, Sarah Holmes
pmc-11688967.description: Approximately half of nursing home residents and 42% of assisted living residents have a diagnosis of dementia. The quality of care that staff provide to long-term care (LTC) residents living with dementia (RLWD) is vital for their well-being. However, questions remain about what strategies staff use to support person-centered dementia care and whether differences exist by length of tenure.

pmc-12594469.description: AudienceEmergency medicine residents and medical studentsIntroductionMany emergency medicine residency programs have their residents take an in-training exam (ITE) in which performance has been linked to certifying exam pass rates, so solid preparation is important.1 The typical clinical schedule of an emergency medicine resident is incredibly varied and time-consuming, which limits time to dedicate to preparation.

pmc-12765092.title: Cognition is associated with daily-life mobility in people with Parkinson’s disease
pmc-12765092.creator: Pablo I. Burgos, Carla Silva-Batista, Anjanibhargavi Ragothaman, Vrutangkumar V. Shah, Patricia Carlson-Kuhta, Fay B. Horak, Martina Mancini
pmc-12765092.description: Highlights•People with PD with poor visuospatial abilities walked slower and with shorter strides.•People with PD with poor executive function had longer double support time.•Poor executive function was also associated with reduced variability in turning performance.•Disease duration and age had a stronger influence on the relationship between cognition and mobility than FoG status.

pmc-12958825.title: Genome-wide evolutionary characterization and expression analysis of the AT-HOOK MOTIF CONTAINING NUCLEAR LOCALIZED gene family in Brachypodium distachyon
pmc-12958825.creator: Jessica Ortiz-Eriamiatoe, Xin Xin, John A Hadish, Michael M Neff
pmc-12958825.description: Plants adapt to diverse environments through complex gene regulatory networks, with the AT-HOOK MOTIF CONTAINING NUCLEAR LOCALIZED (AHL) gene family playing a crucial role. This research identified and examined the AHL gene family within Brachypodium distachyon, a model plant for Pooideae grasses including essential cereal crops.

pmc-13460590.title: A two-stage unified Bayesian framework for adolescent physical fitness surveillance in Sichuan, China: Latent factor measurement followed by spatiotemporal modeling
pmc-13460590.creator: Honglei Wei, Haoran Li, Maowu Pu, Zhou He, Yiru Wang
pmc-13460590.description: Large-scale adolescent fitness testing produces heterogeneous multi-item measurements. Translating these measurements into interpretable and comparable evidence for provincial surveillance remains challenging. We propose a two-stage Bayesian framework for adolescent physical fitness surveillance in Sichuan, China. In Stage 1, Bayesian confirmatory factor analysis maps cross-grade test items onto four latent fitness factors: strength, speed, endurance, and flexibility.

pmc-13556776.title: 544. Associations between mental health–related factors and quality of life in patients with breast cancer: a cross-sectional tudy
pmc-13556776.creator: H Park, B Lee, K Kim, H Suh, H Lim, E Moon, T Kang
pmc-13556776.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBreast cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies among women worldwide, and advances in early detection and treatment have substantially improved survival rates. Consequently, quality of life has emerged as a critical outcome in breast cancer care. Beyond the physical burden of cancer and its treatment, patients frequently experience psychiatric problems, including anxiety, depression, sleep disturbances, and elevated perceived stress. In addition, social support and health-related behaviors, such as alcohol use, may further influence overall well-being.

pmc-13623315.title: Outcomes following varicocele treatment: a comparative study of microsurgical and angioembolization approaches
pmc-13623315.creator: Ammar Al Homsi, Omar Almidani, Fadi Youness, Rashed Rowaiee, Ali Alabdullah, Omar Aljasmi, Ayman Moussa, Kashif Siddiqi, Alaeddin Barham, Omer Raheem
pmc-13623315.description: The aim of this study was to compare outcomes of microsurgical varicocelectomy (MV) versus percutaneous angioembolization (AE) in men with varicoceles causing infertility or scrotal pain. Endpoints included postoperative changes in semen parameters, complication rates, pain relief, need for additional interventions, and the influence of body mass index (BMI).
